taste.name: Imagem viva atrás do vidro, escurecida só sob o controle
taste.trigger: When the designers faced controls that must stay legible on top of a bright photo without turning the whole photo gray
taste.decision: Chose a full-colour photograph with a local dimming band only under each control over a uniform tint or a dark overlay on the whole stage
taste.reason: Because people read the glass as glass only when they can still recognise what sits behind it; a global tint makes the photo look like wallpaper and the control look like a sticker
evidence: Photos stage 808x576px with 3 landscape photos (1.50:1 and 0.67:1)
page chrome is neutral #F4F4F8 on 62.2% of the area
Clarity slider runs Clear to Tinted at 50% default
page text: 'Only the bands under the controls are dimmed, so the image stays bright'

taste.name: Refração e opacidade como parâmetros do usuário
taste.trigger: When the designers faced a material that looks right for one person and blinding or illegible for another
taste.decision: Chose to expose the material as settings (Clarity, Reduce transparency, Reduce bright effects, Show control borders, Optical refraction, Edge displacement 14px) over locking a single intensity as the brand look
taste.reason: Because transparency has a comfort limit that differs by eyes, screen and content, and a tool that cannot be dialled down gets switched off entirely
evidence: 6 settings across 2 panels in the 272px column with 24px radius
caption states the fallback: Chromium bends the backdrop at the edge, Safari and Firefox use the diffuse material

taste.name: Cápsula única e luz no filete, sem relevo
taste.trigger: When the designers faced the temptation to make controls feel raised with layered shadows, gradients and coloured glows
taste.decision: Chose one single-layer shadow (0 10px 30px at 12% black) plus a 1px inner highlight (0 1px 0 white at 92%) and one pill radius over multi-layer elevation, tinted shadows or mixed corner radii
taste.reason: Because a raised, coloured button reads as an object on the page, while a thin rim of light on a transparent pill reads as the edge of a pane of glass
evidence: 51 nodes at 9999px radius, 17 at 3.36e7px, only 4 at 24px
shadows are pure black at 0.12, 0.2 and 0.072 alpha, not tinted

taste.name: Vidros que se fundem num só material
taste.trigger: When the designers faced several glass controls sitting next to each other
taste.decision: Chose a shared backdrop that merges nearby shapes into one contour over drawing every pill as an isolated sticker
taste.reason: Because glass is one continuous sheet in the physical world, and merging tells the eye that these controls belong to the same action group
evidence: 'Separate, then come together' stage ~804x240px with three circular controls and a Bring together button
page text: 'Labels stay sharp while a shared backdrop follows the merging shapes'
scale 0.3s and height 0.2s use a 20-point spring linear() curve
evidence is partly textual: the merge itself was not measured in the DOM
